solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: O for the means to disseminate information!

definitions.text: O for the means to disseminate information!

parts.note: surface reading: the round shape of this character is a ring-shaped symbol of the alphabet
setter's reading: a notice sent round to many recipients at once to spread news

explanation.walkthrough: The 'O for...' looks like a wistful exclamation, wishing for a way to spread news; but the O itself is literally a round character of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A mailing sent in identical copies to a whole list of people is the standard way an organisation spreads notices widely.

clue.text: Uniformed employee in firm, initially managing task on river

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: what comes initially is at the very start, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: first letter of managing
a mission is an assigned task
the Aire is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A uniformed worker at a company is starting out on a job somewhere along a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' in a down clue means the following piece sits beneath, so the river comes last. The Aire is a river in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A commissionaire is a doorman or attendant in livery at a hotel, cinema or office building, so a worker wearing uniform.

clue.text: Sappers given vehicle to prepare for further use

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, the British army's sappers, are abbreviated RE
a bicycle is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Army engineers are handed a vehicle to get it ready for another round of service.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are military engineers; in crosswords they are almost always RE, the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To recycle something is to process or treat waste material so it can be used again.

clue.text: Subject to terrible end in ancient city

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it, enclosed

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so these letters are messed up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An ancient city meets a dreadful fate.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur is the crossword's favourite ancient city; the rearranged NDE goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being under someone's control means being subject to them, as in under orders or under the law.

clue.text: Cancelled article withdrawn from yearbook was the best

indicators.note: withdrawing something from a source takes it out, so those letters disappear

parts.note: an annual is a book published once a year
the indefinite article, removed
someone who led was ahead of everybody else

explanation.surface: A piece pulled from a yearbook turns out to have been its finest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a magazine piece in the surface, but it is just the letter A, and either A in the yearbook word may go.
explanation.definitionFit: Something annulled has been declared void or invalid, which is a formal way of saying it was cancelled.

clue.text: Outhouse of slender construction, excessively short

indicators.note: a word that is short falls a little shy of full length, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: lean means thin, of slender build
too means excessively, as in too much

explanation.surface: A garden shed so flimsily built that it came out far too small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Construction' reads as building work, but here it means build or physique, so slender construction is just lean.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a small shed or outbuilding whose roof rests against the wall of a bigger building.

clue.text: Wrongly cite touring superstar mostly attractive to viewers

indicators.note: to go touring is to travel all round something, so one part wraps around another
doing something wrongly gets it out of order, so these letters must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: mostly means not entirely, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: a legend is a superstar of their field

explanation.surface: A misquoted touring celebrity who still looks great on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: The superstar is trimmed, the four-letter word is jumbled, and the jumble then wraps around the trimmed star.
explanation.definitionFit: Telegenic describes a person who looks good and comes across well on television, appealing to the watching audience.

clue.text: Honour over in Kiel, Bonn, etc

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning something over flips it so it reads from bottom to top
the answer is sitting in the run of words that follows, spanning the word breaks

parts.note: the letters run across the end of Kiel, all of Bonn and the start of etc

explanation.surface: Distinctions conferred across German cities like Kiel and Bonn.
explanation.walkthrough: The German city names are a list of places, but they only supply a string of letters that reads backwards up the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble someone is to raise them to the nobility or to dignify them, a way of conferring distinction.

clue.text: Masterminds seeing Latin Lit translated

indicators.note: translating turns words into another form, so the letters come out rearranged

parts.note: all fourteen letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: Brainboxes reading Latin literature in translation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seeing' looks like a link word joining definition to wordplay, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The intelligentsia are a society's intellectual class, its thinkers and scholars, so collectively the brilliant minds.

clue.text: European state's obsession involving church function

indicators.note: to involve is to take in or include, so one part surrounds another

parts.note: a mania is an obsession
CE is the Church of England
a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: A country's fixation with a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' suggests a purpose, or a church service; here it is a party. Both short pieces go inside the obsession.
explanation.definitionFit: Macedonia, now officially North Macedonia, is a Balkan republic and therefore a sovereign country in Europe.

clue.text: One who stirred up revolution in large square to the west

indicators.note: west is leftward on a map, so in an across clue the letters travel right to left

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A revolutionary agitator in a big town square somewhere in the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' is a number, not a plaza: nine is three squared. The large and square run backwards together to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Lenin led the Bolsheviks in the Russian Revolution of 1917, so he was a man who stirred up a revolt.

clue.text: Risk backing old police force and its area of activity

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the letters are read right to left

parts.note: the Royal Ulster Constabulary, Northern Ireland's police until 2001
NI is Northern Ireland, where that force operated

explanation.surface: Supporting a disbanded police force, and its patch, is a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: The RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, replaced in 2001; 'its area' therefore points to NI, Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur something is to bring it on yourself, so to risk incurring a loss or penalty, as a verb meaning run the chance.

clue.text: Inclined to trap game, inviting legal action

indicators.note: trapping something catches and holds it, so one part encloses the other

parts.note: liable means likely or inclined to do something
tig is the British name for the playground chasing game tag

explanation.surface: Someone tempted to snare game and so laying themselves open to a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' suggests animals to poach, but it is the playground game tig, the British word for tag.
explanation.definitionFit: Something litigable can be contested in court, so a dispute that invites a lawsuit.

clue.text: Like some churches, requiring expensive form of light

parts.note: a steep price is a high one
an LED, light-emitting diode, is a kind of lamp

explanation.surface: Some churches need costly lighting.
explanation.walkthrough: The church electricity bill is a red herring: the pieces are a price adjective and a modern bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: A steepled church has a tall pointed tower, a spire, rising above it, as many parish churches do.

clue.text: Cheap device for identifying stream by church

indicators.note: by means beside or next to, so the pieces are placed side by side

parts.note: a PIN, personal identification number, proves who you are
CH is the abbreviation for church
a beck is a northern English word for a brook

explanation.surface: An inexpensive gadget for spotting which brook flows past the church.
explanation.walkthrough: A beck is a small stream in the dialect of northern England; 'device for identifying' is a number you type at a cash machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinchbeck was a copper-zinc alloy imitating gold, so as an adjective it means sham, tawdry or of little value.

clue.text: Temper displayed by athlete finally breaking record

indicators.note: breaking into something means forcing a way inside, so one piece is put within the other

parts.note: an annal is a yearly historical record

indicators.note: what comes finally is at the very end, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of athlete

explanation.surface: A sprinter loses their cool at the moment of smashing a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temper' looks like anger, but it is the metalworker's verb. Record is not a world record but an annal, a chronicle entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To anneal metal or glass is to heat it and cool it slowly to toughen it, the same process smiths call tempering.

clue.text: Solitary person's high honour featured in article abroad

indicators.note: something featured in a work appears within it, so it is enclosed

parts.note: le is the French definite article
one's is the possessive of one, a person
the Order of Merit, a top British honour

explanation.surface: A recluse's top award appears in a foreign newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solitary person's' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at Solitary. The OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour restricted to 24 living members.
explanation.definitionFit: Lonesome means alone and lonely, feeling isolated from company, just as solitary describes being by oneself.

clue.text: Rings protractedly for tea

parts.note: each O is a ring shape
long means at length, for an extended time

explanation.surface: Someone telephones at great length to order a cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rings' is a phone call in the surface, but it means circles, each one the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Oolong is a Chinese variety of tea, partly fermented, between green and black in character.

clue.text: Ungainly politician, one in luxurious environment

indicators.note: being in a surrounding means being enclosed by it, so these pieces sit inside the other

parts.note: lush means luxurious, opulent
a Member of Parliament
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A clumsy MP living in the lap of luxury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Environment' is the container signal's partner: the luxurious word is what surrounds MP and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumpish means heavy, clumsy and awkward in movement, like a lump, which is what ungainly describes.

clue.text: Spotted animal setter possibly observed on train

indicators.note: in an across clue, putting one thing on another means placing it after, so the pieces join in sequence

parts.note: to coach someone is to train them
a setter is one breed of dog, hence possibly

explanation.surface: A dog breed glimpsed riding on a railway train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' tempts thoughts of the crossword compiler, and 'train' a railway; they are a gundog breed and a verb. A coach dog ran alongside horse-drawn carriages.
explanation.definitionFit: Coach dog is an old name for the Dalmatian, the white breed with black spots that ran beside carriages.

clue.text: Art work produced by French couturier with a university degree

parts.note: Christian Dior, the Paris fashion designer
taken as written
a Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A piece of art made by a Paris fashion designer who holds a degree.
explanation.walkthrough: The couturier is Christian Dior; he is followed by A and an MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional scene with modelled figures set before a painted backdrop, as seen in museums.

clue.text: Uproar engendered by American supporting scrum

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece holds up the other from beneath, so it comes second

parts.note: a ruck is a rugby scrum-like loose maul for the ball
US is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Chaos breaks out when a US fan backs a rugby pack.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby a ruck is the loose scramble for the ball on the ground, much like a scrum; US sits under it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruckus is a noisy commotion or row, a mainly American word for a disturbance.

clue.text: An old railway hotel by river providing charitable accommodation?

indicators.note: by means next to, so the pieces stand side by side

parts.note: the indefinite article
the London, Midland and Scottish Railway, merged into British Railways in 1948
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire, and another in East Anglia

explanation.surface: A disused railway hotel beside a river turned into a refuge for the poor.
explanation.walkthrough: The LMS was one of Britain's four big railway companies before nationalisation. The question mark flags that the definition is descriptive rather than a dictionary entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An almshouse is a home founded by a charity where poor or elderly people may live free or cheaply.

clue.text: Lacerated round back of rosebush — by this?

definitions.text: Lacerated round back of rosebush — by this?

indicators.note: to go round something is to encircle it, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: lacerated flesh is torn

indicators.note: the back of a word is its tail end, so only its last letter is used

parts.note: last letter of rosebush

explanation.surface: Scratched while reaching round the far side of a rose bush, and the culprit is asked about.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole the clue describes the answer: a prick from a rose bush tears your skin. The wordplay puts H inside TORN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose bush carries sharp prickles along its stems, the classic cause of scratched hands for gardeners.

clue.text: Row about grand creature of the forests

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A quarrel over a magnificent woodland beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' rhymes with cow in the surface, a quarrel; it is the other row, a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigers are big cats living mainly in the jungles and woodlands of Asia, so an animal of the forest.

clue.text: River in east with hot flowing water?

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river

indicators.note: something flowing is fluid and on the move, so these letters shift into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for east
H for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A river in the east of a country, full of hot running water.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious German river is right, but the definition is the dialect word: in Somerset a rhine is a drainage ditch, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: On the Somerset Levels a rhine (or rhyne) is a drainage channel or watercourse, so a stretch of water.

clue.text: Fail to be a turncoat, we hear? It's intrusive

indicators.note: what we hear is the sound of words spoken, not their spelling

parts.note: to grass is British slang for informing on others to the police

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to inform on their mates, and called a nuisance for it.
explanation.walkthrough: A grass is British slang for a police informer, and to grass is to betray; failing to do that is NOT GRASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotgrass is a weed of gardens and waste ground that spreads aggressively and is hard to eradicate, an invasive plant.

clue.text: Bard's work stirs writer primarily active around district

parts.note: to shake is to stir up

indicators.note: one thing set around another encloses it

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
an area is a district

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of active

explanation.surface: The Bard's writing moves an author into vigorous local activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' is the pen, not an author; it goes around the district, and the first letter of active closes.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeareana is the collected writings, editions and memorabilia concerning Shakespeare, the poet called the Bard.
